Both are good; the choice mostly depends on how much “server-state management” you expect the app to need.

Use **SWR** if you want a small, simple fetching layer. It is great for “read this resource, cache it, revalidate it” flows, especially in apps that mostly display data. The API is compact, the mental model is easy, and it pairs nicely with Next.js-style patterns. The tradeoff is that once you need lots of mutations, optimistic updates, pagination/infinite queries, cache coordination, retries, or complex invalidation, you may end up building more conventions yourself.

Use **React Query / TanStack Query** if your app has meaningful server state: many endpoints, mutations, filters, background refetching, dependent queries, pagination, optimistic updates, offline-ish behavior, or shared cache invalidation across screens. It gives you more primitives, better devtools, richer mutation handling, and a very mature ecosystem. The tradeoff is slightly more API surface and more decisions up front.

My default recommendation: **choose TanStack Query** for a new React app unless the app is very lightweight. It scales better as data flows get messy, and the extra structure pays for itself quickly.

Quick rule of thumb:

| Need | Pick |
|---|---|
| Simple reads, minimal setup | SWR |
| Dashboard/admin/product app | TanStack Query |
| Lots of mutations | TanStack Query |
| Optimistic updates | TanStack Query |
| Tiny app or mostly static pages | SWR |
| You want the smallest mental model | SWR |
| You want batteries included | TanStack Query |

One practical note: whichever you choose, keep fetch logic behind small hooks like `useUser`, `useProjects`, `useUpdateProject`. That way the choice stays replaceable instead of leaking through the whole app.

Both are good. I’d choose based on how much “server-state machinery” your app needs.

Use **SWR** if your app mostly needs simple read-heavy fetching: dashboards, settings pages, profile data, lightweight CRUD, or Next.js-style UI where stale-while-revalidate feels natural. It has a smaller API surface, is easy to teach, and gets you caching, deduping, revalidation, focus refresh, and optimistic updates without much ceremony.

Use **React Query**, now **TanStack Query**, if you expect more complex data flows: lots of mutations, dependent queries, pagination/infinite scroll, background refetching rules, cache invalidation, retries, offline-ish behavior, or many screens sharing server state. It is more opinionated and feature-rich, with excellent devtools and stronger primitives for mutation/invalidation workflows.

Main tradeoffs:

| Area | SWR | TanStack Query |
|---|---|---|
| Learning curve | Smaller, simpler | Larger, more concepts |
| Mutations | Works, but lighter-weight | Stronger mutation + invalidation model |
| Cache control | Simple global cache | More explicit, powerful query cache |
| Pagination/infinite queries | Possible | First-class support |
| Devtools | More limited | Excellent |
| Bundle/API surface | Leaner | Heavier but more capable |
| Best fit | Simple fetching | Full server-state management |

My default recommendation: **use TanStack Query** for a new React app unless you’re intentionally keeping the app very simple. It scales better as requirements grow, and the mutation/invalidation model pays for itself quickly.

Pick **SWR** if you want the least conceptual overhead and your data fetching is mostly “load this resource, keep it fresh.”
